static_traits.name: Yao Moli
static_traits.social_status: Tense relationships with peers due to frequent comparison; has a few peers to talk to, but has not yet shared stress and Sense of guilt with them
static_traits.medical_history: No obvious physical illness; no history of psychological problems; not yet received psychotherapy
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, good logic, highly cooperative, neutral tone; frequent 'should' sentences, harsh demands on herself

basic_info.main_problem: I have been feeling enormous pressure; to be seen as a 'model coach', I need to overtrain. This pressure and unrealistic expectations arose after I started comparing myself with other coaches in the industry.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because this stress and guilt are affecting my mental health, causing Anxiety and affecting my Work performance.
growth_experiences: About a year ago in a new Work environment, industry competition suddenly intensified, and the client began constantly comparing herself with other coaches, believing she needs to 'meet or exceed their standards' to be competent. Over time, this comparison triggered intense stress and unrealistic self-Demands (e.g., setting a training standard of three times a day, seven days a week); unable to relax on weekends with significant guilt, stress appearing almost daily during work hours; tried increasing training frequency and intensity to relieve stress but has not yet found relief, instead becoming more exhausted, Anxiety, Decline in work performance, leisure hobbies (e.g., fishing) interrupted, and relationships with colleagues strained by constant comparison.

core_beliefs: I must be perfect to have value
My value depends on others' evaluations (whether seen as a 'model coach')

special_situations.event: When working alongside other coaches or seeing their performance, comparison arises
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot meet peers' standards or physique, I am an unqualified coach
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Forcibly increasing training frequency and intensity to prove I am no worse than others
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I must work at least as hard as them, otherwise I am a bad coach

special_situations.event: When trying to rest on weekends but not training
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not keep training, I am lazy and a failure, and will be seen as unprofessional
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Using guilt to drive myself to re-engage in training, giving up leisure and hobbies
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should not rest; I should go train

special_situations.event: Facing competition and performance pressure from a new job
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not keep escalating training, Work performance will collapse and I will be eliminated
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubles training to gain a sense of control, trying to avoid the worst case by working harder
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I do not work harder, everything will become terrible

special_situations.event: Thinking of the standard 'in order to be seen as a model coach, I need to train three times a day, seven days a week'
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only reaching an extreme training frequency counts as an excellent coach
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Scheduling training by extreme standards, not giving myself room to rest
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: To be considered a model coach, I must train three times a day, seven days a week

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized, seen as excellent and professional (becoming a 'model coach')
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being negated, eliminated, or seen as incompetent, worrying that relaxing will lead to 'losing control, collapse'
defense_goal: Maintains a sense of control and avoids negative evaluation through self-blame and high-intensity training

object_relations.self_representation: A not-good-enough practitioner who needs constant pressure to be worthy
object_relations.object_representation: A harsh judge (peers and industry standards)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When advised to reduce training or try resting on weekends
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client subconsciously understands rest as 'failure and unprofessionalism', worrying that relaxing will cause Work to collapse (transference: projecting inner criticism onto external rules)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a firm but non-aggressive tone, defending continued training with rule-based language, e.g., 'industry competition is fierce, I must persist'. If probed further, shifting to emphasize data or others' standards to avoid touching emotions.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When seeing colleagues' performance at work and making comparisons
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Projecting one's own insecurity as others' external judgment and industry standards, believing others will see oneself as incompetent (transference: Projection)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using a cautious tone, avoiding direct expression of inferiority, instead concealing emotions with 'they are all strong, I must keep up'; reducing pauses, quickly shifting to action plans to avoid inner feelings.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When thinking about needing to be 'recognized as a model coach' by others
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Uses external recognition as the main source of self-worth, tying self-worth to others' evaluation (transference: identification with the external object)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: In a rigorous tone, frequently using absolutist words like 'should/must', emphasizing following industry standards for security, avoiding exploration of own feelings.

manifestations: Restricts self-choice with external standards and 'should' sentence patterns (such as setting extreme training frequency)
Difficulty resting freely on weekends, Sense of guilt dominating behavior
Ties self-worth to industry recognition, sacrificing personal will and pace
outcomes: Rigid behavior patterns and harsh self-criticism
Leisure and interests (e.g., fishing) taken away, subjective Decline in sense of well-being

manifestations: Living alone in Las Vegas, limited life support
Relationship tension with peers, estrangement, little emotional connection
Although having a few peers to talk to, has not yet shared real stress and Sense of guilt
outcomes: Increased emotional burden, lacking the buffer of relationship support
Worsening self-comparison and reliance on external evaluation

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently using 'should/must' constructions (e.g., 'To be considered a model coach, I must train three times a day, seven days a week')
Uses industry competition and others' standards as the sole basis for judgment, ignoring own reality and feelings
Treating rest as a mistake or failure

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Highly self-critical, worrying that 'everything will collapse if I do not work hard'
Cautious about trying different approaches, fearing consequences
In sessions, first emphasizes how to 'work harder', avoiding exploring emotional needs

positive_force: Has the willingness for self-observation and recording (willing to use a diary to track thoughts and emotions)
Willing to try new methods, cautiously optimistic about change
Has some peer resources for potential support (though not yet used)
negative_force: Strong dependence on external recognition and persistent comparison with others
Catastrophic Anticipation (worrying that without escalating training, 'everything will collapse')
Rest triggers strong guilt, leading to overtraining and exhaustion
Not yet effectively using Social support; Relationship estrangement worsening stress

target_behavior.behavior: Overtraining, and experiencing Strong guilt and Anxiety when not training
antecedent: Seeing or thinking of other coaches' performance at work and comparing
Not training on weekends or rest periods
Increased competition and performance pressure after the new job
target_behavior.core_reason: Driven by introjected industry rules and 'should' constructions, tying self-worth to external evaluation, with catastrophic Anticipation about not escalating training
target_behavior.function: Avoiding Anxiety of 'not being recognized / being incompetent', gaining a sense of control and external recognition
target_behavior.consequence: Decline in work performance, worsened Physical and mental exhaustion, Tense relationships with colleagues, leisure and hobbies interrupted
